family_history: No family history of aneurysm or SAH

patient.chief_complaint: Sudden onset severe headache this morning, vomiting, neck stiffness
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. Chen is a 48-year-old Asian female with a history of hypertension presenting to the emergency department with a sudden onset severe headache that began approximately 6 hours prior to arrival. She reports she was preparing breakfast when she developed an instantaneous, explosive headache she rates as 10/10 in severity, unlike any headache she has experienced before. She vomited twice before her husband brought her to the emergency department. She denies any preceding warning headache or sentinel event. She reports photophobia and phonophobia since onset. She initially attributed it to stress but her husband noticed she seemed confused briefly right after the onset, though she appears cognitively intact now on arrival. She reports mild ongoing neck pain and stiffness. She denies focal weakness, visual changes, speech difficulties, or loss of consciousness. She has no personal history of migraines or recurrent headaches. Her blood pressure has been controlled on her current regimen per her last primary care visit 2 months ago. She denies any recent trauma, recent illness, or new medications. She reports no exertion or Valsalva maneuver at the time of onset - it came on spontaneously at rest.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4; GCS 15; mild irritability; photophobic; appropriate responses
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: PERRL 3mm bilateral, brisk; no ptosis; EOM intact; no papilledema; visual fields full by confrontation
neurological_exam.motor: 5/5 strength upper and lower extremities; no pronator drift
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch and pinprick
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ symmetric throughout; plantar responses flexor bilaterally
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-nose-finger intact; rapid alternating movements intact
neurological_exam.additional: Nuchal rigidity present - chin-to-chest restricted approximately 3 cm; Kernig sign positive bilaterally; Hunt-Hess Grade 2

findings.description: Moderate hyperdense blood filling suprasellar cistern, interpeduncular fossa
Small amount of blood layering in third ventricle

additional_observations: Mild hydrocephalus - temporal horns mildly dilated
ct.impression: Moderate subarachnoid hemorrhage with blood in basal cisterns, bilateral Sylvian fissures, and small intraventricular extension (third ventricle). Fisher grade 3. Mild early hydrocephalus. Consistent with aneurysmal SAH. CTA urgently required.

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: WBC 14.6 x10^9/L (H), Glucose 162 mg/dL (H), Troponin I 0.22 ng/mL (H), BNP 186 pg/mL (H).

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 28 cmH2O. WBC: 210 (corrected) (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 195 mg/dL. Glucose: 88 mg/dL (serum 162, ratio 0.54 - normal) (ratio 0.54). Xanthochromia: Present - yellow discoloration visually apparent. Spectrophotometry: Bilirubin peak confirmed.

findings: Deep symmetric T-wave inversions in leads I, aVL, V2-V6
QTc prolongation to 512 ms - risk of Torsades de Pointes

findings.finding: Small irregular aneurysm 5.2 x 4.8 mm with bilobed morphology; neck 2.8 mm
findings.status: Likely ruptured based on distribution of hemorrhage

output.impression: Bilobed 5.2 mm anterior communicating artery aneurysm consistent with ruptured aneurysm - distribution of basal cistern blood supports AComA origin. Conventional DSA recommended for definitive characterization and treatment.
recommended_actions: Neurovascular surgery team review for coiling vs clipping decision

quantitative_data.clinical_correlation: Patient c/o worsening headache and mild confusion

output.impression: Day 4 TCD showing mild bilateral MCA vasospasm (MFV 142, 128 cm/s) with borderline Lindegaard ratios suggesting onset of early symptomatic vasospasm. Continue nimodipine, optimize euvolemia, consider CT perfusion if clinical deterioration.

output.wall_motion: Apical akinesis with basal hyperkinesis - Takotsubo pattern
findings: Apical ballooning pattern consistent with Takotsubo stress cardiomyopathy
output.impression: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (neurogenic) associated with SAH. EF reduced to 45%. Monitor; expect recovery over weeks.

findings.description: Bilateral MCA territory CBF reduced to 28-32 mL/100g/min (normal >45)
Perfusion mismatch suggesting penumbra at risk but no established infarct

output.impression: CT perfusion shows bilateral MCA territory hypoperfusion consistent with moderate vasospasm-induced delayed cerebral ischemia. Penumbra at risk but no infarction yet. Urgent intervention required.

output.proposed: Nimodipine 60 mg orally every 4 hours x 21 days
interactions: Amlodipine + nimodipine: additive calcium channel blockade - monitor blood pressure carefully
warnings: Hold amlodipine during nimodipine course to avoid excessive hypotension
Never crush capsules for IV use
Monitor BP before each dose - hold if SBP <100

output.query: Subarachnoid hemorrhage vasospasm prevention nimodipine outcome

results.finding: Nimodipine 60 mg q4h x21 days reduces poor neurological outcome by 34%
Class I recommendation for oral nimodipine; triple-H therapy for symptomatic vasospasm
Simvastatin did not reduce vasospasm or improve outcomes in SAH

output.summary: Oral nimodipine 60 mg q4h for 21 days is standard of care for vasospasm prevention (Level I evidence). Triple-H therapy (hypertension, hypervolemia, hemodilution) for symptomatic vasospasm. TCD monitoring days 4-14. CT perfusion for objective vasospasm assessment. Intra-arterial therapy (verapamil, angioplasty) for refractory cases.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from anterior communicating artery aneurysm (Hunt-Hess 2, Fisher 3)

differential.key_features: CT shows blood, CSF non-clearing bloody with xanthochromia
CTA shows saccular aneurysm not beading pattern; CSF diagnostic of SAH
CSF bloody without neutrophilic pleocytosis; no fever; normal glucose ratio
No sellar mass on CT/CTA; no visual field defects; no hormonal abnormalities

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Fisher grade 3 SAH in basal cisterns with IVH
Deep T-wave inversions, QTc 512 ms - avoid QT-prolonging drugs
Mild troponin elevation, stress leukocytosis - consistent with neurogenic cardiac injury

optimal_actions.action: Lumbar puncture (if CT equivocal) - confirmatory xanthochromia
CTA head and neck for aneurysm localization
Start nimodipine 60 mg q4h x21 days
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Hold amlodipine to avoid additive hypotension

critical_actions: Urgent CT head to confirm SAH
CTA for aneurysm identification and treatment planning
ICU admission with continuous cardiac monitoring (QTc 512 ms - arrhythmia risk)
Monitor sodium daily - cerebral salt wasting risk
contraindicated_actions: Do not give QT-prolonging medications (haloperidol, metoclopramide, ondansetron) given QTc 512 ms
Do not anticoagulate or give antiplatelet agents before aneurysm is secured
Do not allow uncontrolled hypertension before aneurysm treatment (rebleeding risk)
key_reasoning_points: Fisher grade 3 SAH with IVH carries higher vasospasm risk than grade 2 - daily TCD monitoring essential days 4-14
AComA aneurysms are the most common cause of SAH and often present with basal cistern blood distribution
QTc prolongation to 512 ms in SAH requires avoidance of QT-prolonging drugs and continuous cardiac monitoring
Neurogenic Takotsubo cardiomyopathy occurs in 10-30% of SAH and is managed supportively
Intraventricular extension of hemorrhage increases hydrocephalus risk - monitor for ICP elevation
Mild transient confusion at onset (witnessed by husband) suggests brief vasospasm or ICP spike at aneurysm rupture
Nimodipine improves outcomes via reducing vasospasm severity - Level I evidence from multiple RCTs
